items.abstract: Abstract The interfacial adhesion between carbon fibers and polymer matrices critically determines the mechanical performance of fiber-reinforced composites, yet achieving strong bonding remains a persistent challenge. A molecular engineering strategy is developed to tailor the fiber-matrix interphase in carbon fiber-reinforced poly(arylene sulfide sulfone) (PASS) composites by designing three sizing agents: poly(amic acid) (PAA) and its thermally imidized polyimide derivatives bearing either ether or sulfone groups. Through a combined experimental and computational approach, the influence of the chemical structure of the sizing agents─specifically, the nature of the groups (ether vs sulfone), and the postimidization state-on interfacial adhesion and failure behavior is systematically investigated. The results demonstrate that the sulfone-containing polyimide sizing agent exhibits superior interfacial reinforcement, which is attributed to its strong intermolecular interactions with the PASS matrix, including hydrogen bonding as well as π-π stacking enabled by its rigid, conjugated chain architecture. items.abstract: Abstract To address the degradation issues of conventional polyimides under high-temperature and high-field energy storage conditions, this study synthesized a semi-aromatic polyimide featuring both hydrogen-bonding and chemically cross-linked networks. The chemically cross-linked structure anchors the high-temperature-resistant segments, while the dynamic hydrogen bonds further restrict chain mobility and provide additional charge trapping sites, which may contribute to shortening the mean free path of electrons and suppressing long-range carrier transport. Molecular dynamics simulations and X-ray diffraction indicate that the interchain distance shortens from 4.66 Å to 4.18 Å, with a corresponding decrease in free volume and thermal expansion coefficient. TSDC testing shows that the trap depth increases from 1.08 eV to 1.14 eV, and the leakage current density is as low as 1.98×10-7 A cm-2 at 200 MV m-1. Finally, the discharge energy density of the bis-crosslinked semi-aromatic PI reached 6.63 J cm-3 and 4.80 J cm-3 at 150 °C and 200 °C, respectively, with an efficiency >90%, and a maximum energy density of 5.08 J cm-3 at 250 °C (87.3% efficiency). items.abstract: Abstract Integrating optically thin metasurfaces with continuous-wave (CW) terahertz sources offers an alternative to conventional bulky optical elements for manipulating terahertz waves. However, planar optical elements composed of metasurfaces have yet to be actively adopted in CW terahertz sources due to limited fabrication methods suitable for micrometer-scale meta-atoms. Here, we fabricate two types of printed terahertz collimating metalenses on cyclo-olefin polymer and polyimide films using super inkjet printing. The fabricated metalenses are composed of double-sided printed metal patches on dielectric films, enabling simultaneous control of the electric and magnetic fields while maintaining an optically thin structure. The printed terahertz collimating metalenses fabricated on cyclo-olefin polymer and polyimide films enhance the directivity of a resonant tunneling diode oscillating at 0.312 THz to 2.29 and 1.46 times, respectively. items.abstract: Abstract As next-generation high-frequency communication technologies advance rapidly, microelectronic components require higher processing temperatures and reduced signal loss. Consequently, poly(ester imides) (PEIs) are widely utilized in these fields. However, efficient recycling methodologies for PEIs remain to be established. In this work, we developed a PEI chemical recycling protocol via glycolysis. The proposed system was verified as generally applicable to depolymerizing various types of PEIs. Moreover, the depolymerization process enabled the isolation of aromatic diols: bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) and 5-hydroxy-2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)isoindoline-1,3-dione (HPID). While the recovered BHET established a closed-loop polyester recycling pathway within the glycolysis system, the isolated HPID was converted into aromatic diamine to serve as a precursor for regenerating high-performance PEIs. items.title: Phthalonitrile-Terminated Polyimide Adhesives with Benzimidazole-Promoted Curing for High-Temperature Bonding
items.abstract: Abstract A heat-resistant phthalonitrile-terminated polyimide (PN–PI) adhesive was developed by blending long and short poly(amic acid) chains. The short chains contain benzimidazole units that promote phthalonitrile (PN) end-group curing, while amide units in the long chains provide polar sites for intermolecular and interfacial interactions. Isoquinoline lowers the imidization temperature, allowing ring closure to finish before extensive PN curing. Within the examined composition range, PI3 exhibits a glass transition temperature (Tg) of 347.2 °C, with lap-shear strengths of 18.35 MPa at room temperature and 10.02 MPa during short-term testing at 300 °C. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations show stronger bulk cohesion in short-chain-rich systems, whereas PI3 gives the most negative interaction energy with Al(111). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal an electron-rich benzimidazole nitrogen, supporting its possible role in PN curing. The combined regulation of chain composition and benzimidazole-promoted PN curing provides a PN–PI adhesive with strong bonding performance at 300 °C.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT To overcome the conflict between sustained thermal insulation and electromagnetic wave transparency under extreme conditions, this work designs a bilayer fluorinated aerogel composite. The outer layer consists of a unidirectional fluorinated polyimide (FPI) aerogel with a rigid molecular skeleton, whose porous architecture delivers low thermal conductivity (39.6 mW m −1 K −1 )), high porosity (91.9%), an ultra‐low dielectric constant (1.039), and hydrophobicity (water contact angle: 124.6°). The inner layer is a fluorination‐modified poly(vinyl alcohol) aerogel embedded with silica‐encapsulated phase‐change microcapsules as thermal buffers, offering a high latent heat capacity (153.8 J g −1 ), maintained porosity (76.7%), and a low dielectric constant (1.26) while ensuring leakage‐free thermal cycling. The combination of the two layers provides a gradient thermal protection: the outer layer suppresses steady‐state heat conduction, while the inner layer buffers transient thermal shocks through latent heat absorption. items.title: High-Temperature Dielectric Energy Storage in All-Organic Composite Films Enabled by Molecular Semiconductor Fillers
items.abstract: Abstract Polymer dielectrics suffer from severe conduction losses under coupled thermal-electrical stresses, limiting their practical applications in film capacitors under harsh conditions. Incorporation of organic molecular semiconductor fillers with concurrently high electron affinity (Ea) and large bandgap (Eg) into the polymer matrix represents a promising modification strategy, although only limited semiconductor fillers have been reported. Here, we report an all-organic high-temperature dielectric composite where an alternative molecular semiconductor tetracyanobenzene characterized by an Ea of 3.92 eV and Eg of 4.65 eV is used. Experimental results demonstrate that the trap density is significantly increased, which effectively suppresses leakage current and leads to a marked enhancement in breakdown strength. Consequently, the polyimide-based composite film exhibits a high discharged energy density (6.92 J cm–3) with a high charge–discharge efficiency (90.32%) at 150 °C. This outperforms most currently existing all-organic and nanocomposite dielectric polymers, thereby offering a facile yet effective strategy for the design of high-temperature dielectric polymers.

items.title: Mechanical Ruggedization of Ceramic Column Grid Array with Polyimide Reinforced Solder Columns
items.abstract: Recent advancements in Area Array Packaging (AAP) utilize Ceramic Column Grid Arrays (CCGAs) to provide high-density interconnects for printed circuit boards that can improve reliability in harsh environments compared to traditional Ball Grid Array (BGA) architectures. However, CCGA assemblies can still experience premature failure, often manifesting as crack propagation induced by shear loading to the column when packages are exposed to severe thermal cycling and prolonged vibration. This work demonstrates the feasibility of a novel method using polyimide tubing to mechanically reinforce individual solder columns to improve shock and vibration robustness and reduce the risk of Foreign Object Damage (FOD). Alternative approaches, including corner staking and 3-D printed reinforcement, are limited by increased board space consumption and manufacturing difficulty. A process for manufacturing polyimide-reinforced solder columns has been defined, as well as methodology for attaching them to a ceramic package.

items.title: A polyimide-based thermal bridge
items.abstract: Thermal management across micro- to macro-scale critically depends on accurate characterization of intermediate-scale materials, such as individual fibers and thin films. Yet, measuring the thermal conductivity of a single fiber remains rather challenging. Here, we present a polyimide (PI)-based thermal bridge for accurate thermal transport measurement of single fibers and related microscale samples. By addressing key challenges in hybrid material integration and flexible substrate interconnection, our approach retains the mechanical flexibility of PI while achieving compatibility with conventional microfabrication processes. The PI suspension beams exhibit thermal conductance of ∼12 μW K−1, within one order of magnitude of similar devices made of SiNx, while their vertical stiffness is more than two orders of magnitude higher, providing exceptional stability for sample manipulation. items.abstract: Polyimide (PI) films are widely used in semiconductor packaging, but their measured mechanical response can vary depending on the moisture conditions maintained during testing. In this study, the tensile behavior of moisture-conditioned PI films was compared using conventional ex-situ and a proposed in-situ tensile testing method. Water absorption tests, tensile tests, cross-sectional observations, and finite element analysis were conducted to evaluate the influence of the testing environment. The PI film exhibited near-Fickian moisture absorption behavior, reaching an equilibrium water uptake of approximately 2.7 wt% after 24 hours of immersion. The ex-situ specimens maintained ultimate tensile strengths of approximately 250–265 MPa, comparable to the room-condition value of 251 MPa, while their fracture strains decreased to 0.22–0.30. Research on the Patterning Polyimide Layer Based on Laser Ablation Technology
items.abstract: Polyimide (PI) has emerged as a critical material in advanced semiconductor packaging owing to its high temperature stability, low dielectric constant and loss, mechanical flexibility and stress relief, and chemical and moisture resistance. The passivation (PA) layer is usually formed by polyimide-based lithography technology during the whole process of IC packaging, such as bumping packaging, fan-in wafer-level packaging (FIWLP), and fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP). A study on the patterning of a polyimide layer based on laser ablation technology is introduced in this manuscript. A series of samples with the structure of Si substrate/PI layer were prepared, and four different laser ablation conditions were applied to these samples. An inverted trapezoid shape of the opening structure was observed in the PI layer after the effect of laser ablation, which also indicated that the top width was about 6.4 ± 0.6 μm larger than the bottom width according to the measurement data based on scanning electron microscopy (SEM). items.title: A Review of CMOS-Compatible Flexible Biosensors Based on Polymer Electronics for Wearable Healthcare
items.abstract: Flexible wearable biosensors have emerged as a promising technology for continuous, noninvasive health monitoring, driven by the growing demand for personalized healthcare and an aging global population. Polymeric substrates such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyimide (PI), and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) provide lightweight, flexible, and low-cost platforms that conform to the human body, but their practical deployment requires reliable integration with complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) electronics for signal acquisition, processing, and wireless communication. This review summarizes recent advances in CMOS-compatible flexible biosensors, emphasizing polymer-based sensing platforms, circuit-level integration, and system-on-chip (SoC) architectures for wearable healthcare applications. Flexible sensing mechanisms, including electrochemical, capacitive, resistive, and transistor-based devices, are discussed alongside CMOS analog front-end circuits, low-noise amplifiers, analog-to-digital converters, and ultra-low-power signal conditioning techniques. items.title: Tailoring the Orientation of Electron‐Delocalized Conjugated Structures in Polyimide Dielectrics for High‐Temperature Capacitive Energy Storage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Dielectric polymers for high‐temperature capacitive energy storage require both high thermal stability and electrical insulation. Although the rigid conjugated structure of polyimide affords a high glass transition temperature, making it a promising candidate, it also introduces compromised electrical insulation through electron delocalization. Here, we propose and demonstrate that regulating the spatial orientation of localized π‐containing/electron‐delocalized conjugated structures in polyimide can effectively break the trade‐off between thermal stability and electrical insulation. The out‐of‐plane orientation of localized conjugated structures reduces the spatial connectivity of short‐range electron‐delocalization sites along the electric‐field direction, thereby suppressing continuous carrier migration. items.abstract: Abstract Additive manufacturing represents a versatile platform for the development of high-frequency communication electronics. However, existing dielectric polymer inks often fail to simultaneously meet the requirements of low dielectric loss, high thermal stability, and high mechanical robustness. In this work, a photosensitive polyimide (PSPI) was synthesized via an acrylate-grafting acyl chlorination route, incorporating trifluoromethyl, bulky fluorene, and asymmetric diphenyl ether moieties. This molecular architecture facilitates the formation of a highly cross-linked network (with a gel content of up to 94%) and enables solvent-free 3D printing while ensuring ultralow dielectric loss and high thermal stability. The cured PSPI ink exhibits a glass transition temperature of 170 °C and a tensile strength of 71.42 MPa. items.abstract: Abstract The increased interest in the development of sustainable materials for printed electronics necessitates durability studies in their operating environments. Hence, in this paper, the effects of photodegradation on five different nanocellulose and four reference substrates were examined. items.abstract: Photosensitive polymer films are used in semiconductor manufacturing as dielectric and passivation layers. Their chemical, mechanical, and interfacial properties depend not only on the total exposure dose applied, but also on the temporal characteristics of the exposure, which influence the photochemical reaction kinetics and the formation of the polymer network. Industrial exposure tools deliver the same dose with different intensity–time profiles. It remains an open question whether the commonly held assumption of exposure reciprocity applies to chemically complex systems such as high-performance polyimides. items.abstract: Carbon fiber (CF) is renowned for its exceptional mechanical properties; however, its inherent surface inertness and susceptibility to processing damage frequently compromise interfacial adhesion with polymer matrices. Sizing treatment serves as an effective and industrially scalable strategy to overcome this limitation. This review systematically examines the protective and thermodynamic roles of sizing agents, the four fundamental interfacial mechanisms of chemical bonding, mechanical interlocking, physical adsorption, and interphase formation, alongside the specific characterization techniques employed to analyze them. items.abstract: Epoxy resins are widely used in electronic packaging and electrical insulation, but their permanent cross-linked networks and low intrinsic thermal conductivity restrict material recycling and heat dissipation. In this work, a recyclable epoxy composite was developed by combining a dual-dynamic epoxy network with silica-coated poly(p-phenylene benzobisoxazole) fibers. items.abstract: ABSTRACT Surface metallization of polyimide (PI) films is essential for constructing conductive electrodes and interconnects in flexible electronics, directly determining device integration and reliability. However, the high inertness and low surface energy of PI necessitate complex pretreatment in conventional vacuum deposition, incurring high costs and substrate damage, while wet etching faces environmental burdens and poor compatibility, both failing to meet large‐scale manufacturing demands. Inspired by the stable coordination of histidine in Nereis jaws, a coordination‐directed molecular design strategy is proposed. By introducing nitrogen‐containing heterocyclic units into PI molecular chains, intrinsic metal anchoring sites are constructed, enabling direct film metallization without destructive adhesion‐promoting surface pretreatments. This process integrates with photolithography, printing, and direct writing for cross‐scale controllable metallization, fabricating planar wiring and vertical interconnect access (VIA) structures for 3D high‐density integration. items.title: Strain control of mid-IR spectroscopic nonlinear photocurrents in PtSe$_2$
items.abstract: Semi-metallic noble-metal dichalcogenides are promising materials for infrared optoelectronics, yet the origin and tunability of their nonlinear optical responses remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate in-situ mechanical control of photon-drag photocurrents in polycrystalline PtSe$_2$ thin films grown on flexible polyimide substrates. Using polarization-resolved mid-infrared photocurrent spectroscopy under uniaxial tensile strain, we observe pronounced strain-dependent changes in resistivity, photoconductivity, and helicity-dependent nonlinear photocurrents. The spectral response is consistent with optical excitations across the spin-orbit-coupling-induced (SOC) band gap near the K point. We develop a theoretical framework attributing the photocurrent primarily to photon-drag induced by photon-momentum symmetry breaking. Strain modifies its magnitude and polarization dependence through deformation potentials that tune the SOC-induced band gap. These results establish mechanical strain as a route toward reconfigurable infrared polarization detection.

items.abstract: This study presents a CMOS-compatible, fully integrated three-dimensional island-bridge concept for flexible electronics on silicon planar technology. By embedding metal bridges within trenches in a polyimide-passivated island matrix, the approach localizes mechanical stress to the bridges whereby active components on the islands are protected from mechanical stress, enabling high-performance thin-film transistors (TFTs) on flexible substrates. A concave, arc-shape forming fill in trenches between the islands and backside etching yield freestanding 3D bridges. items.title: Inkjet Printed Interconnections on Flexible Substrates
items.abstract: Utilization of inkjet printing as a manufacturing method in electronics has been studied at Tampere University of Technology. In order to successfully utilize inkjet deposited circuit patterns with traditional electronics components, different aspects must be considered. One of the critical issues is the electrical contact between discrete components and inkjet printed conductive traces. In this study, discrete passive components were joined to conductive traces that were inkjet printed with metalloorganic nano silver ink on flexible substrates such as polyimide foil and polyethylene naphthalate (PEN). JEDEC 22-A104C Standard temperature cycling tests as well as shear strength tests were carried out on the manufactured samples. items.abstract: The rapid development of flexible displays has spurred the rational design and performance optimization of colorless polyimide films (CPI) with superior integrated properties.
